title: Permissions inventory — endpoint & job audit (coverage + gaps)
content:
Context
- This is the working audit used during Discovery (RBAC v2) to enumerate security-relevant endpoints + background jobs, flag missing/weak authorization checks, and propose a canonical permission mapping.
- Source-of-truth for final catalog will be Confluence “permission inventory and classification”. This doc is the messy coverage spreadsheet we used to get there.
- Scope: Hosted API gateway routes, Control Plane service endpoints, Console/admin backend endpoints, and platform jobs that mutate customer state.

Conventions used in this audit (WIP)
- Permission format (proposed): ri.<domain>.<resource>.<action>.v1
  - Example: ri.org.api_keys.rotate.v1
  - NOTE: align final strings with ADR-014 (naming/versioning). If ADR requires different separators, we’ll mechanically transform.
- Sensitivity tiers
  - T0: non-sensitive read (docs/health)
  - T1: customer read-only (view configs, list resources)
  - T2: customer write (create/update configs)
  - T3: admin / access control / policy changes (roles, routing policies, retention)
  - T4: secrets / key material / break-glass / audit export (high impact)
- “Existing authz” column legend
  - NONE = no explicit authz check found (or only authn)
  - V1 coarse = RBAC v1 role gate (org_admin etc.) or “isOwner” checks
  - Mixed = check exists but inconsistent across codepaths (gateway vs service) or bypassable via alternative route
  - V2 annotated = endpoint has explicit permission annotation / registry entry (post-PR-28188 style)
- Expected error semantics (target)
  - 401: unauthenticated / invalid token
  - 403: authenticated but not authorized (include denial code internally; optional debug header for admins)
  - 404: only for truly not-found (avoid using 404 to “hide” authz failures unless explicitly designed)

High-level summary (as of 2025-02-04)
- Endpoints/jobs reviewed: 63
  - Control Plane: 34
  - API Gateway (Hosted API): 14
  - Console/admin backend: 11
  - Background jobs / internal ops: 4
- Coverage status (rough)
  - Explicit check present (v1 or v2): 41
  - Missing check entirely: 12
  - Mixed / inconsistent across routes: 10
- Error semantics issues
  - Uses 404 on authz failure: 7 endpoints
  - Returns 200 + “success:false” style (legacy): 2 endpoints
  - Uses 500 on deny (throws): 3 endpoints
- Priority findings
  1) Streaming chat route had an authz bypass via alternate handler (see incident + hotfix reference; separate ticket)
  2) Audit export paths are inconsistent between Hosted vs Private (permission mismatch + 404-on-deny)
  3) Routing policy edit/update is gated by org_admin in some services but not in “apply/publish” job
  4) Role binding write endpoints allow read of current bindings without consistent scope checks (project/env scoping)

Open questions / TODOs
- Scope semantics: for routing policies + model pinning, is scope Org or Project or Environment? Current implementations assume Org; Private asks for Cluster/Environment scoping.
- Console “permission viewer”: do we show raw permission strings or friendly labels? (impacts how we name permissions; keep human-readable)
- Should audit export require a dedicated “audit.export” permission in addition to “audit.read”? (lean yes)
- Deprecation: how long do we maintain v1 role gates as fallback in dual-read?

Background jobs / internal operations
050 | Job | routing-publisher | routing-policy-publish-job | n/a | T3 | ri.routing.policies.publish.v1 | NONE | n/a | Job runs as service account; must still enforce “who initiated” at request time and record initiator in job payload + audit event. | Diego Santos | P0
051 | Job | audit-exporter | audit-export-s3-job | n/a | T4 | ri.audit.export.create.v1 | Mixed | n/a | Ensure job only runs for authorized export requests; log authz decision context into exported record for evidence.
052 | Job | key-rotation | api-key-rotation-worker | n/a | T4 | ri.org.api_keys.rotate.v1 | NONE | n/a | Rotation can be invoked by API; job must verify request had permission and not allow direct internal trigger without check.
053 | Job | private-installer | private-bootstrap-admin-job | n/a | T4 | ri.private.bootstrap_admin.execute.v1 | NONE | n/a | Needs strong controls + alerts (break-glass style). Determine if we gate behind installer token + org admin + explicit permission.

Notes on recommended fixes (grouped)
A) Deny-by-default middleware + annotations
- Any endpoint touching T3/T4 must be annotated with a permission and covered by deny-by-default enforcement (gateway and service interceptor).
- Add CI guard: fail if a new T3/T4 endpoint ships without an annotation.

B) Normalize error semantics
- Remove 404-on-deny unless we explicitly choose “resource hiding” and document it.
- Avoid “200 success:false” legacy patterns.
- Ensure denial reason codes exist internally; optionally expose debug header to org admins / support (see PR for debug header approach).

C) Split coarse permissions
- Routing: separate update vs publish.
- RBAC: separate roles.* from role_bindings.*
- Secrets: separate list metadata vs read value (and strongly consider not supporting read value at all).
- Audit: separate read vs export.

D) Audit logging requirements
- For any T3/T4 action: ensure audit event includes
  - subject (user/service account), orgId, scope, action (permission string), decision (allow/deny), denial code (if deny), policy version/hash
  - resource identifiers when applicable (keyId, roleId, policyId)

Next steps (what we need from owners)
- Each P0 item: confirm endpoint owner + target permission string + enforcement layer (gateway/service/both).
- Platform Eng to turn this audit into a tracked coverage report tied to PRs:
  - Permission registry entries (PR-28134)
  - Gateway middleware enforcement (PR-28159)
  - Control Plane annotations (PR-28188)
  - Integration tests for critical paths (upcoming)

Changelog
- 2025-01-17: initial endpoint scrape (Hosted + Control Plane)
- 2025-01-24: added Console/admin backend endpoints + first error-semantics pass
- 2025-02-04: added background jobs + flagged P0 gaps (routing publish, audit export, secrets, private bootstrap)
